messages:
alex_t: quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel routing change i noticed a ~12% drop in prefix cache hit-rate for a subset of traffic. reproduces on canary.
priya_g: ugh. any obvious diffs in cache keys? or is this kv eviction due to batching changes?
samir: looked at the traces — keys are mostly intact, but there are many near-duplicates that differ only by a tiny system prompt suffix. maybe canonicalization mismatch.
lina: to confirm: we recently switched kernel selection to prefer nhead-optimized kernels for short sequences. that path appends a small debug flag to system prompt when traced, could that leak into keying?
alex_t: yes — the tracing middleware was adding "\n#kernel=nhead-opt" to system_prompt in debug mode. it shouldn't, but it did for 1% of requests. keys include the whole serialized prompt block.
priya_g: that matches: if system prompt content changes even by whitespace or a flag, cache keys diverge. we need to ensure keying normalizes or excludes ephemeral metadata.
samir: profiling also shows KV cache warmup is slower for the affected hosts — fewer prefix hits means larger KV growth + more compute. cost perf hit visible in p50 latency.
perf-bot: perf-regression-alert: prefix_cache_hit_rate decreased from 0.78 to 0.69 for canary group (window=30m). Investigating bins: user-facing prompts with tool/call metadata most affected.
lina: proposal: update cache keying rules to (1) strip any lines starting with "#kernel=" and any trailing debug comments, (2) canonicalize system_prompt whitespace (trim + single spaces), and (3) ignore ephemeral tool-internal fields like "_trace_id" when serializing tool/function call arguments for keys.
alex_t: agree. also add tokenizer/version pin into the key (model + tokenizer_hash) — we saw a tiny fraction of hits mismatch across tokenizer upgrades.
priya_g: careful: adding tokenizer hash increases cardinality; but it's necessary for correctness. maybe include only major-version hash (e.g., vocab id) not micro-build id.
samir: alternative: attach a key-version field separate from prompt fingerprint, so we can roll forward keys without invalidating old cache entries unexpectedly. e.g. cache_meta: {"key_schema_version":"v2"}
lina: i like key-schema-version approach. then normalization rules are part of the schema and rollouts can migrate.
alex_t: immediate steps:
- patch tracing middleware to not mutate system_prompt (hotfix) — samir
- deploy normalization layer in front of cache key generation (strip kernel flags, normalize whitespace) — priya
- include tokenizer major-vocab-id in meta (not raw build hash) — lina
- run synthetic warmup to validate hit-rate before full canary rollback — alex
priya_g: i'll push normalization + unit tests. will add a small fuzz harness that generates prompt variants with instrument flags to ensure deterministic keys.
samir: i'll revert the debug flag in kernel routing on canary now.
perf-bot: task-note: create alert rule to catch sudden ->10% drop in prefix hit-rate per release. tag: infra/perf
lina: long-term: we should audit all code paths that serialize tool/function args. we've seen several libs add ephemeral fields (timestamp, request_id) which leak into keys. add a whitelist for stable keys.
alex_t: agreed. one more thing — batching heuristics changed tokenization boundaries for some prompts; we should record tokenizer version and tokenizer-normalized text used for key derivation in traces so we can debug without blowing up cardinality in the cache.
priya_g: good call. i'll add a non-indexed trace field e.g. "probe:tokenized_fingerprint" with a short digest.
samir: ok patch + revert in flight. i'll post updates in this thread when canary metrics look green.
alex_t: thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
priya_g: pushed normalization PR, tests green. link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/+/1234
lina: canary metrics at +10m: prefix_hit_rate recovering to 0.76. still shy of baseline but heading in right direction.
alex_t: closing loop: we'll keep key-schema-version v2 for this change and schedule a follow-up to migrate stale entries or TTL tune. moving to close once canary is stable.
